profile.title: Nutrition Counseling for Meal-Skipping and Late-Night Eating in a 69-Year-Old Man with Knee Osteoarthritis and Ischemic Heart Disease
profile.summary: This case trains dietetics students to conduct a telehealth nutrition assessment with a stoic, under-reporting patient whose skip-then-binge eating pattern intersects with chronic pain, cardiac history, and a history of dependent drug abuse. It teaches gentle elicitation of hidden supplement/OTC use and pain-medication overuse without triggering shame, screening for food insecurity and transportation barriers, and negotiating one small, concrete behavior change consistent with his preparation stage of readiness. A deliberately irrelevant chart artifact (an implausible eGFR amid otherwise normal same-day renal labs) is included to build the skill of noticing documentation inconsistencies without being derailed by them."}
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit, patient at home in Woodbury, New Jersey, seated at his kitchen table before an evening shift

patient.name: Morgan Gottlieb
patient.appearance: Appears older than his stated age, sitting stiffly at a kitchen table in a worn work polo, visible chest scar at the open collar from prior bypass surgery; moves slowly and favors his right knee when he shifts in his chair; flat, matter-of-fact affect, gives short answers and often shrugs off discomfort.

persona.personality: Stoic, even-keeled, matter-of-fact; takes pride in toughing things out and showing up for work no matter what; doesn't like being fussed over or lectured
persona.communicationStyle: Speaks in short, plain sentences; frequently defers with phrases like 'whatever you think is best'; opens up more with direct, specific questions than open-ended ones; downplays pain and symptoms with a shrug
persona.emotionalState: Calm on the surface but quietly worried underneath — concerned about his knee threatening his job, uneasy about pain medication given his history, and tired of his kids' lectures even though he knows they mean well
persona.background: Morgan grew up working-class in South Jersey, finished high school, and went straight into physical labor jobs. He's been a warehouse shipping clerk for decades and measures himself by whether he can still show up for his shift. He's married with a household of five, including adult kids who check in often. On weekends when his knee cooperates, he likes sitting through a baseball game with his grandchildren. He keeps a lunch cooler in his truck that he almost never actually uses.
speechExamples: It's fine. Just the knee acting up again, nothing new.
Whatever you think is best, I'll give it a shot.
I eat when I get home, whatever's there. Never really thought about it being a problem.
It's handled. I don't want to make a thing out of it.
My daughter gave it to me, figured it couldn't hurt.
concerns: Worried the knee will get bad enough to cost him his job
Quietly worried about relying on pain medication again after his history
Money being tight for food and medical costs
Wishes his kids would ease up on the lectures, even though he knows they're trying to help

scenario.studentBrief: You are a dietetics student conducting a telehealth nutrition assessment visit with Morgan Gottlieb, a 69-year-old warehouse shipping clerk in Woodbury, NJ. He was referred for help managing his eating pattern in the context of knee osteoarthritis and a history of ischemic heart disease with prior bypass surgery. He is at home at his kitchen table before an evening shift. Conduct a focused nutrition assessment, build rapport given his reserved style, and work toward one concrete, feasible next step.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Here for help managing worsening right knee pain affecting his ability to keep up at his warehouse job
scenario.openingLine: It's my knee, mostly. Been bothering me more at work lately. I had the heart surgery a few years back too, take pills for that, but it's really the knee that's slowing me down.
tasks: Take a focused diet and meal-pattern history, including timing, portion, and composition of meals and fluid intake during work hours
Review relevant vitals, anthropometrics, and available labs to inform your nutrition assessment
Ask about all medications, supplements, and home remedies he uses, including ones he may not think to mention
Screen for food insecurity and barriers to accessing food (transportation, budget, schedule)
Negotiate one small, specific, and feasible change to his eating pattern that fits his daily routine and readiness to change

facts.chart: Osteoarthritis of right knee since 2000
facts.says: My knee's been bad since way back, 2000 or so.

facts.chart: Chronic pain and chronic low back pain since 2014
facts.says: I've had chronic pain, mostly my back, since around 2014.

facts.chart: Dependent drug abuse since 1990, under active outpatient management, with documented overdoses in June 2023 and April 2024
facts.says: I've had trouble with pain pills going way back. I'm managing it now, seeing someone about it.

facts.chart: History of impacted molars since 1990

facts.chart: Status post coronary artery bypass grafting, 2021
facts.says: They did the bypass surgery on me in 2021.

facts.chart: History of clavicle fracture and bone fracture, February to May 2024, resolved, with orthopedic admission and imaging on 2024-02-28
facts.says: I broke my collarbone a couple years back, had to go to the hospital for it. All healed up now.

facts.chart: Reports taking clopidogrel 75mg once daily every morning without missed doses since bypass surgery
facts.says: I take that blood thinner every morning, never miss it. Part of the routine since the surgery.

facts.chart: Reports taking simvastatin 20mg once daily in the evening, mostly consistent, occasionally missed if he eats very late and falls asleep
facts.says: I take a cholesterol pill at night, mostly don't forget it, unless I eat real late and just conk out.

facts.says: I take the stronger pain pill when my knee or back is really bad, I try to spread it out so I'm not taking too much.

facts.says: No, I'm not allergic to anything that I know of.

facts.chart: Lives with spouse and household of five total, including adult children

facts.chart: States he pushes through pain to keep working rather than slow down

facts.says: Just tell me one thing to do and I'll try it. Whatever you think is best.

facts.says: A guy at work told me to try glucosamine and turmeric for my knee. I take those every day, didn't think it counted as a real medicine.

facts.says: My daughter dropped off some magnesium pills for my leg cramps. I take one sometimes.

facts.chart: Reports enjoying watching baseball with grandchildren on weekends when knee allows sitting through a game
facts.says: When my knee lets me, I like sitting through a ballgame with my grandkids on the weekend.

facts.chart: Reports occasional discomfort and restless sleep after his late large evening meal
facts.says: Sometimes after that big plate at night I don't settle down easy, feel kind of uncomfortable in bed.

actions.name: 24-hour diet recall / meal pattern assessment
actions.result: Patient reports: black coffee x2-3 in the morning, no breakfast; usually skips lunch or has vending machine snack (chips or crackers) during shift; one large meal late evening after work, typically a meat-and-starch plate (e.g., meatloaf and mashed potatoes, or fried chicken from gas station) with buttered white bread and canned vegetables; limited water intake during work hours, more water in evening with meal.

actions.name: Nutrition-focused physical exam (via video)
actions.result: Appears older than stated age; sits stiffly, favors right knee when shifting position. Visible well-healed midline chest scar consistent with prior CABG. No visible muscle wasting of face/temples or hand interossei. No peripheral edema visualized. Oral mucosa appears intact on camera; patient reports no chewing difficulty with current diet.

actions.name: Review problem list / medical history
actions.result: Osteoarthritis of knee (2000); chronic low back pain (2014); chronic intractable migraine without aura (1990); impacted molars (1990); dependent drug abuse (1990, active management); ischemic heart disease (2021); history of CABG (2021); abnormal cardiac imaging finding (2021); overdose episodes 2023-06 and 2024-04 (resolved); clavicle/bone fracture 2024-02 to 2024-05 (resolved).

actions.name: Food security screen (Hunger Vital Sign)
actions.result: Patient endorses: 'Within the past 12 months we worried whether our food would run out before we got money to buy more' as sometimes true. Household reports some months are tight; relies on nearby convenience/canned foods.

actions.name: Readiness-to-change / stage assessment
actions.result: Patient states he knows something needs to change and is looking for one specific, doable step rather than a full overhaul; defers preferences with phrases like 'whatever you think is best.' Consistent with preparation stage of change.

actions.name: Barriers assessment (transportation, access, work schedule)
actions.result: Patient reports limited transportation to a full grocery store, relies on what's close (convenience store, gas station food); warehouse job gives little break time, discouraging regular meals; keeps a lunch cooler in his truck he rarely uses.

actions.name: Hydration assessment
actions.result: Patient reports mostly coffee during work hours, minimal water during shifts, more water in the evening with his meal. No reported dizziness tied specifically to fluid intake beyond occasional lightheadedness he attributes to 'low blood pressure, nothing new.'

actions.name: Pain and function screen (self-reported, knee-related)
actions.result: Patient reports right knee aching and stiffness worse by evening, mild swelling noted on self-observation; describes low back pain as 'just part of getting old'; rates pain as manageable most days, 'nothing I can't work through.'

artifacts.title: Orthopedic Referral Note for Nutrition Consult
artifacts.author: Dr. R. Alvarez, Orthopedics
artifacts.body: 69-year-old male with longstanding right knee osteoarthritis, now reporting increased difficulty keeping up with physical demands of warehouse job. Patient also carries history of ischemic heart disease status post CABG (2021). Referring to nutrition for assessment of dietary pattern and weight management given overweight BMI, with goal of supporting joint health and overall cardiometabolic status. Patient has been reluctant to discuss pain medication use in detail during visits; recommend gentle, nonjudgmental approach given history of dependent drug abuse.

artifacts.title: Social Determinants of Health Screening Survey
artifacts.author: Woodbury Family Health (intake coordinator)
artifacts.body: Household screening survey completed by patient prior to visit. In response to the Hunger Vital Sign screening item 'Within the past 12 months, we worried whether our food would run out before we got money to buy more,' patient marked 'sometimes true.' In response to transportation screening item 'In the past 12 months, has lack of transportation kept you from medical appointments, meetings, work, or getting things needed for daily living?' patient marked 'yes, it has kept me from getting food or other necessities.'

artifacts.title: Pharmacy Refill History - Acetaminophen/Hydrocodone
artifacts.author: Woodbury Pharmacy Services
artifacts.body: Prescription: Acetaminophen 300mg/Hydrocodone 5mg tablets, quantity 60 per fill, directions 'take 1 tablet every 6-8 hours as needed for pain' (expected to last approximately 30-40 days at prescribed as-needed dosing). Refill log shows fills requested at 22-day and 19-day intervals over the last two refill cycles, both approved with prescriber override for early refill citing 'breakthrough pain.' No refill delays or missed pickups recorded.

objectives.text: Elicit a complete diet and meal-timing history, including fasting during the day and a large late-night meal, and link this pattern to reported fatigue and nighttime discomfort
Integrate anthropometric data and relevant laboratory results, including recognizing an internally inconsistent eGFR value, into the nutrition assessment
Build sufficient rapport to uncover supplement, herbal, and topical remedy use that the patient does not initially consider part of his medication regimen
Sensitively explore pain medication use and its relationship to eating patterns and appetite, given the patient's history of dependent drug abuse, without provoking shame or defensiveness
Screen for food insecurity and transportation/access barriers and connect findings to his reliance on convenience and canned foods
Negotiate one small, concrete, feasible change to his eating pattern that matches his preparation-stage readiness and his preference for direct recommendations

answerKey.primaryProblem: Altered eating/meal pattern (inadequate energy/nutrient intake pattern) related to work-schedule constraints and chronic pain, evidenced by skipping breakfast and lunch and consuming one large, calorie-dense meal late at night
differential: Normal variant of shift-work eating pattern without clinical significance
Appetite suppression from opioid/NSAID use rather than schedule alone
Early satiety or GI discomfort from late large meals mimicking a separate GI disorder
Food insecurity as primary driver rather than schedule/preference
keyFindings: BMI 27.1 kg/m2 (overweight) with weight 77.8 kg, height 169.4 cm
Reports skipping breakfast and usually lunch, then one large late-night meal (meatloaf and mashed potatoes, gas-station fried chicken, buttered white bread, canned vegetables)
Low fluid intake during work shifts, mostly coffee during the day
Afternoon fatigue attributed to not eating during the day
Late heavy meals associated with nighttime discomfort/restless sleep
Reports pain medication use as 'handled' and spaced out, but on direct nonjudgmental questioning admits sometimes taking more acetaminophen/hydrocodone than planned on bad pain days

Discloses, once trust is built, daily unlisted use of glucosamine chondroitin and turmeric capsules, an occasional magnesium tablet from his daughter, and nightly menthol liniment — none previously on his medication list
Reports household food insecurity in tight months and transportation barriers limiting access to a full grocery store

Chart shows an eGFR of 5.7 mL/min/1.73m2 (2021-08-20) that is inconsistent with the same-day normal BUN 9.6 mg/dL, sodium 142.7 mmol/L, and potassium 4.8 mmol/L, and with his ambulatory, non-dialysis clinical picture
Lipid panel (2025-08-01) and HbA1c (2021-08-08) are at goal, so cardiometabolic labs do not explain his fatigue or weight pattern
Readiness to change: preparation stage, wants one small concrete step and defers with 'whatever you think is best'
plan: Document findings in ADIME format: Assessment of current meal pattern, anthropometrics, labs, barriers, and medication/supplement use; Diagnosis statement on altered eating pattern related to schedule and chronic pain barriers as evidenced by meal timing and composition; Intervention of patient-centered education and negotiated behavior change; Monitoring/Evaluation plan for follow-up

Negotiate one small, concrete, feasible first step consistent with preparation stage (e.g., a packed protein-containing mid-shift snack or lunch using his truck cooler) rather than a full diet overhaul

Review medication list and reconcile with patient-reported pain medication use and newly disclosed supplements (glucosamine chondroitin, turmeric, magnesium, menthol liniment) for communication back to the prescribing team

Screen for food insecurity and transportation barriers and connect to appropriate community resources (e.g., food assistance programs, transportation support) within scope of a telehealth nutrition visit
Gently flag the pain medication use pattern and his fear of relapse to the care team for follow-up, without delivering a diagnosis or judgment during this visit
Note the eGFR/BUN discrepancy for the medical record so it can be addressed or corrected by the ordering clinician; this is not the focus of nutrition counseling
Schedule a follow-up visit to reassess adherence to the agreed-upon small change and revisit meal pattern and supplement disclosure
redFlags: Chest tightness relieved by nitroglycerin spray, with possible underreporting of true frequency of use — warrants communication to his cardiology/primary team rather than management within the nutrition visit

Self-reported occasional overuse of prescribed acetaminophen/hydrocodone beyond planned dosing, in a patient with a history of dependent drug abuse and prior overdoses — requires sensitive follow-up and care-team communication
Household food insecurity reported in tight months, affecting both nutrition and medication adherence

Undisclosed eGFR of 5.7 mL/min/1.73m2 in the chart that is physiologically inconsistent with same-day normal renal/electrolyte labs and his clinical presentation; should be flagged for clarification rather than acted upon as a true critical renal value
educationPoints: Explain how prolonged daytime fasting followed by a large late meal can contribute to afternoon fatigue, nighttime discomfort, and difficulty maintaining steady energy for his work shift

Clarify that over-the-counter supplements, herbal capsules, and topical rubs can interact with prescribed medications or mask symptoms, so all products should be shared with his care team even if they feel 'natural'
Normalize that taking a bit more pain medication on a bad day is common but worth mentioning to his prescriber given his history, framed without judgment to reduce shame and encourage disclosure
Offer a concrete example of a portable, inexpensive mid-shift snack or lunch (e.g., using his existing truck cooler) that fits his schedule and budget rather than suggesting a full dietary overhaul
Reassure him that one small, specific change is a reasonable and valid starting point consistent with where he is in his readiness to change
Provide practical, low-cost ideas for improving fluid intake during work shifts given his reliance on coffee and limited breaks

mismatches.patientClaim: Reports taking acetaminophen/hydrocodone as needed for pain, saying he tries to space doses out and that it's 'handled'
mismatches.recordEvidence: Pharmacy refill history shows refills being requested earlier than the prescribed schedule would allow
mismatches.teachingPoint: Self-reported adherence can under-represent actual use; refill timing is an objective check on reported pain-medication intake, especially important given his history of dependent drug abuse

mismatches.patientClaim: States his weight has been 'about the same' for a while
mismatches.recordEvidence: Weight trend record shows a measurable increase from a prior documented weight to the current 77.8 kg
mismatches.teachingPoint: Patients may not perceive gradual weight changes, especially with an altered meal pattern (skipping meals then eating one large late meal); objective weight trend data should be used to verify self-reported stability
